muse_prompt: Beneath an ancient peepal tree with thick textured bark and dense green canopy, an elderly great sage with warm weathered wheat-brown skin, lean ascetic build and deep compassionate brown eyes beneath calm brows rests in upright stillness upon a low circular seat of fresh green kusha grass mats on a raised earthen platform. His long white-grey matted hair gathered in a high topknot and flowing white beard and mustache frame his face marked with white tripundra ash on forehead and arms, while he wears a simple saffron-ochre cotton dhoti with woven rust-gold border and matching angavastram over the left shoulder with white sacred thread across the chest and many rudraksha bead necklaces and bracelets. His bare feet rest on the earth as his wooden danda staff leans beside the platform and a deer skin holds a small wooden kamandalu water pot, rudraksha japa mala and a small clay lamp near a small stone fire altar, bathed in soft golden morning light filtering through leaves. Small bright birds sing softly among the green forest around him as he breathes deep in quiet thought, wrapped in mountain-calm light, seeking the true tale of a perfect good man with serene humble dignity.

In warm golden morning light filtering through dense green leaves, an elderly great sage with warm weathered wheat-brown skin, lean ascetic build, long white-grey matted hair in a high topknot and flowing white beard, wearing a saffron-ochre dhoti with rust-gold border and angavastram over the left shoulder with white sacred thread, rudraksha necklaces and bracelets and white tripundra ash, holding a wooden danda staff in his right hand with a small wooden kamandalu and rudraksha japa mala in his left, gathers three young pupils close around bark-mat seats. The three young brahmachari disciples around twelve to sixteen years old with warm wheat-brown skin, slender builds, calm dark eyes and shaved heads with small black shikha topknots wear simple saffron-ochre dhotis and shoulder cloths with woven red borders, white sacred threads, sandal-paste tilaks and rudraksha beads, each holding a small wooden kamandalu water pot and a bundle of palm leaves with hands folded in humble devotion. Behind them stands a peaceful hermitage cluster of small mud-plastered huts with steep thatched grass roofs and bamboo doors beneath towering banyan and peepal trees, with a central brick yajna fire altar amid tulsi platforms, clay water pots, wooden ladles and young banana and mango saplings. The sage speaks with gentle authority as a radiant sun-wheel emblem glows golden above the leaves, signaling the bright sun line and twenty-four thousand verses carried forward like dawn light, filling the clearing with serene sacred promise and joy.

In the same peaceful hermitage of mud-plastered huts with steep thatched roofs and bamboo doors beneath towering banyan and peepal trees, an elderly great sage with weathered wheat-brown skin, long white-grey topknot, flowing white beard, saffron-ochre dhoti with rust-gold border, angavastram, sacred thread, rudraksha necklaces and tripundra ash tells his tale beside a central brick yajna altar, holding his wooden danda staff. Three young brahmachari disciples twelve to sixteen years old with wheat-brown skin, shaved heads with small black shikha topknots, saffron-ochre dhotis with red borders, sacred threads, sandal tilaks and rudraksha beads listen with folded hands, each with a small kamandalu and palm-leaf bundle. Above and beyond them opens a luminous edgeless vision of a vast deep blue ocean under dawn light, its waters parted around fresh earthen banks, joined with a strong stone foundation emblem of an ancient sun line. Through the glowing vision a mighty rushing river surges forward in swirling currents, carrying the strength of sixty thousand marching currents as living water, bathed in golden morning radiance. Warm light links the quiet foreground storytellers with the shining expanse, filling the air with awe, continuity and mountain-calm power.

In warm golden morning light beneath towering banyan and peepal trees, an elderly great sage with warm weathered wheat-brown skin, long white-grey topknot, flowing white beard, saffron-ochre dhoti with rust-gold border, angavastram over the left shoulder, white sacred thread, rudraksha necklaces and white tripundra ash stands with hands folded together in blessing speech, his wooden danda staff resting against a bark seat with his small kamandalu and japa mala close by. Beside the wide serene Sarayu river under clear luminous sky, vast fertile plains of Kosala glow with golden corn and lush green rice fields edged by flowering groves and mango orchards. Middle-aged men and women of Kosala with warm wheat-brown complexions and gentle dark brown eyes gather among the ripe harvest, the men in pleated cream cotton dhotis with saffron woven borders and shoulder angavastrams with small gold motifs, black hair in neat topknots with sandal paste tilaks and copper bracelets, the women in deep red, turmeric yellow and leaf green cotton sarees with gold butti patterns, long black hair in jasmine-adorned braids with glass bangles, gold earrings and bright bindis. The air shimmers with prosperity and tranquil joy as sunlight bathes the fields in gold.

Honey-golden sandstone palaces with cusped-arch windows, domed chhatris and gilded pavilions draped with saffron pennants rise above crenellated walls with grand red-sandstone torana gateways, while gleaming white marble temples lift tall curvilinear shikharas crowned by golden kalashas in warm dawn light.
